# Jubilees Chapter 30 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Dinah's violation; Simeon and Levi's revenge praised; the absolute ban on intermarriage

---

**30:1** At the start of the forty-fifth jubilee — first week, first year — Jacob arrived safely at Salem, the city near Shechem, in Canaan, coming from Paddan-aram.

**30:2** Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite — the local chieftain — caught sight of Dinah and abducted her. He had sex with her and violated her. She was twelve years old.

**30:3** Afterward, he pressed his father and Dinah's brothers to arrange a formal marriage.

**30:4** Jacob and his sons were enraged by what had been done to their sister. They played along with the negotiations while plotting their revenge.

**30:5** Simeon and Levi struck without warning. They swept through the city and killed every man. They took their sister Dinah and left.

**30:6** Jacob was furious with them. "You've ruined everything," he said. "You've made us enemies of every tribe in this land."

**30:7** But God did not share Jacob's outrage — because Simeon and Levi had acted out of righteous passion. They had avenged what was done to their sister.

**30:8** There is no forgiveness for a man who violates his neighbor's daughter. It is utterly repugnant to God.

**30:9** Israel — meaning Jacob here — actually loved what they had done in his name. They had defended Israel's dignity.

**30:10** The people of Israel are therefore commanded: do not give your daughters in marriage to Gentiles, and do not take Gentile women as wives for your sons. This is impure and abominable in God's sight.

**30:11** Any Israelite who takes a Gentile wife, or who gives his daughter to a Gentile man, is defiled — thoroughly and without exception.

**30:12** Such a union is corruption and ruin and a spreading plague before God.

**30:13** There is no forgiveness, ever, for this sin. The man who commits it will die without children, cut off entirely from his people.

**30:14** This is the same command given to Abraham, to Isaac, to their descendants — observe this law, this statute, this ordinance.

**30:15** It is carved into the heavenly tablets: no defilement through intermarriage. Anyone who does it will be erased.

**30:16** Any line of Israel that intermarries with foreigners — giving daughters or taking foreign women — that family line will be pulled out by the roots.

**30:17** No act of intermarriage shall pollute Israel. It is contamination in every sense.

**30:18** And the foreign nations who violate Israel's daughters? No forgiveness for them either.

**30:19** As for Simeon and Levi — they are inscribed in the heavenly tablets as righteous men. They drove defilement away from Israel.

**30:20** Their names stand forever before the Holy One as righteous. They will be honored in every generation for their zeal for God.

**30:21** It is also recorded in the heavenly tablets concerning Shechem and his men: what they did to Israel came back on them. Their own names are written there for destruction, in every generation.

**30:22** Because of Levi's zeal — his commitment to justice, judgment, and vengeance against Israel's enemies — God gave him the priesthood forever, for himself and his sons.

**30:23** This is why the priesthood belongs to Levi and his sons perpetually. They eat the firstfruits before God, they are exalted, they receive tithes from all Israel and the firstlings of every crop and herd — grain, wine, oil, cattle, sheep.

**30:24** Tell the children of Israel: "Keep this command. It is written forever in the heavenly tablets."

**30:25** If any man violates an Israelite woman, he is to be executed. The heavenly tablets say it plainly: "Bring him out and stone him to death, for he has defiled Israel."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Chapter 30 is the most theologically jarring chapter in Jubilees for modern readers. The author of Jubilees inverts Genesis 34's ambiguous moral framing: where Genesis depicts Jacob's sons acting deceitfully and Jacob criticizing them, Jubilees explicitly states God approved of the killing. This is the "Phinehas model" — righteous zeal that justifies extrajudicial violence in defense of communal purity. The intermarriage prohibition here is the most absolute in any ancient Jewish text.*
